After a successful rename response, the application SHALL display the returned name in the edited member's list row and close the editor. Renaming SHALL leave the selected member ID, identity cookies, onboarding completion and route unchanged. Renaming the selected member SHALL make its updated name available to existing selected-name display behavior.

- **WHEN** a successful rename response updates the currently selected member
- **THEN** its list row displays the returned name and the editor closes

title: Verify the selected release before executing bundle code
raw_body: Installation guidance SHALL identify the official repository, exact release tag, channel, versioned ZIP and SHA-256 checksum asset before bundle code runs. Missing, ambiguous or mismatched evidence SHALL block execution. A checksum from the same release SHALL be described as integrity evidence under that origin's trust, not independent publisher authentication.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Verify the selected release before executing bundle code

Installation guidance SHALL identify the official repository, exact release tag, channel, versioned ZIP and SHA-256 checksum asset before bundle code runs. Missing, ambiguous or mismatched evidence SHALL block execution. A checksum from the same release SHALL be described as integrity evidence under that origin's trust, not independent publisher authentication.

#### Scenario: Select a stable release
- **WHEN** a human or agent starts from the stable download entry point
- **THEN** it resolves one exact release and matching ZIP/checksum pair and records that identity before proceeding
- **AND** later latest-release changes cannot silently substitute another version

#### Scenario: Missing or mismatched checksum
- **WHEN** the checksum is missing, malformed, ambiguous or does not match the selected ZIP bytes
- **THEN** no script from that ZIP is executed and the handoff identifies the failed integrity check and a safe retry action

#### Scenario: Checksum includes a path
- **WHEN** a checksum record carries the publisher's build-directory prefix
- **THEN** verification binds the expected digest to the selected local ZIP without trusting that record to choose arbitrary filesystem paths

#### Scenario: Unapproved origin or channel
- **WHEN** the proposed bundle comes from another repository, an arbitrary download URL or an unselected prerelease
- **THEN** the agent stops for an explicit release selection instead of treating the bundle as the supported stable installation

title: Use only commands and files shipped for the selected release
raw_body: Human and agent paths SHALL use the same versioned templates and existing setup/update helpers. Guidance SHALL distinguish current-release behavior from unreleased mechanics and SHALL establish command support from trusted matching release documentation before invoking new flags. ### Requirement: Use only commands and files shipped for the selected release

Human and agent paths SHALL use the same versioned templates and existing setup/update helpers. Guidance SHALL distinguish current-release behavior from unreleased mechanics and SHALL establish command support from trusted matching release documentation before invoking new flags. A missing contract SHALL require a human handoff, not probing legacy scripts or fabricating a stack.

#### Scenario: Legacy bundled release
- **WHEN** a verified release includes cloudflared in its base Compose file but lacks read-only status flags and scenario overlays
- **THEN** its bundled golden path remains valid and the agent reports structured status unavailable without passing new flags to setup or update

- **WHEN** a verified release actually includes the shared overlay and matching setup/update behavior
- **THEN** shared-mode guidance uses those shipped files, the selected external network and a unique proxy alias without an app-local connector token

- **THEN** it uses an absolute GitHub URL and identifies preview guidance as unreleased

title: Inspect prerequisites without changing the installation
raw_body: Supported helpers SHALL expose an explicit read-only inspection mode for setup and update. It SHALL assess applicable prerequisites, selected files and configuration without collecting secrets, creating configuration/data, pulling images, starting services or changing networks. Missing prerequisites SHALL produce an actionable result instead of automatic installation or privilege escalation.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Inspect prerequisites without changing the installation

Supported helpers SHALL expose an explicit read-only inspection mode for setup and update. It SHALL assess applicable prerequisites, selected files and configuration without collecting secrets, creating configuration/data, pulling images, starting services or changing networks. Missing prerequisites SHALL produce an actionable result instead of automatic installation or privilege escalation.

#### Scenario: Fresh unconfigured project
- **WHEN** read-only setup inspection runs in a verified bundle with no private configuration
- **THEN** it reports prerequisites and the local human configuration handoff without creating .env, generating secrets or creating data directories

#### Scenario: Temporary archive inspection
- **WHEN** update inspection requires scratch files
- **THEN** it uses private disposable space, removes it on exit and leaves installation files unchanged

#### Scenario: Required tool or Docker access unavailable
- **WHEN** Bash/runtime tools, the Compose plugin or authorized Docker access are unavailable
- **THEN** the available inspection or agent handoff identifies the missing prerequisite and human action without sudo, package installation or daemon changes

#### Scenario: Inspect update prerequisites
- **WHEN** read-only update inspection receives a target bundle and backup-evidence path
- **THEN** it reports existing version/configuration compatibility and evidence availability without changing WFS_VERSION or treating that file as proof of recoverability

title: State supported and unqualified environment boundaries
raw_body: Installation assistance SHALL identify the target host, architecture and Docker/Compose method and distinguish the documented Linux Compose path from tested qualification. An unsupported environment or unestablished DSM import behavior SHALL produce a bounded human handoff. It SHALL NOT replace HTTPS requirements or change host security/network configuration to make a check pass.
raw_block:
### Requirement: State supported and unqualified environment boundaries

Installation assistance SHALL identify the target host, architecture and Docker/Compose method and distinguish the documented Linux Compose path from tested qualification. An unsupported environment or unestablished DSM import behavior SHALL produce a bounded human handoff. It SHALL NOT replace HTTPS requirements or change host security/network configuration to make a check pass.

#### Scenario: Synology project import is unqualified
- **WHEN** a shared-template deployment relies on a DSM import honoring COMPOSE_FILE but that behavior is not established
- **THEN** assistance reports the limitation and requests review of the complete project file selection instead of deploying the base alone

#### Scenario: Host platform outside the documented path
- **WHEN** the host is macOS, Windows or an unqualified host configuration
- **THEN** assistance distinguishes source/disposable tests from target-host support and does not claim an install is qualified there

title: Keep secret entry in a local human session
raw_body: The agent SHALL hand credential generation/entry to the human through existing interactive helpers or a private local editor. It SHALL NOT request secrets in chat, accept secret command-line arguments in inspection mode, source dotenv as code or reproduce secrets in output. Agent handoffs SHALL NOT construct secret-bearing commands.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Keep secret entry in a local human session

The agent SHALL hand credential generation/entry to the human through existing interactive helpers or a private local editor. It SHALL NOT request secrets in chat, accept secret command-line arguments in inspection mode, source dotenv as code or reproduce secrets in output. Agent handoffs SHALL NOT construct secret-bearing commands.

#### Scenario: Human configures a new deployment
- **WHEN** a verified bundle is ready for configuration
- **THEN** the human enters credentials locally with agent capture/transcription disabled and the agent receives only a non-secret completion/status result

#### Scenario: Inherited interactive confidentiality limitation
- **WHEN** the human helper uses secret values in subprocess arguments
- **THEN** guidance records the process-list exposure limitation and does not claim hidden prompts eliminate it

- **WHEN** a prerequisite or configuration check fails
- **THEN** status uses allowlisted diagnostics and a local inspection instruction rather than raw child output, resolved Compose configuration, tokens, cookies or secret-derived values

title: Preserve project and storage identity on every handoff
raw_body: Assistance SHALL retain existing project names, directories, private configuration, selected Compose files, volumes and database/file mount identities. ### Requirement: Preserve project and storage identity on every handoff

Assistance SHALL retain existing project names, directories, private configuration, selected Compose files, volumes and database/file mount identities. - **THEN** it reports existing-state review and preserves all bytes instead of rerunning configuration as a fresh install

- **THEN** inspection reports the conflict without choosing an alternative layout or suggesting broad orphan/volume cleanup

- **THEN** only its entry proxy is attached to the external bridge, supporting services retain private networks, and cross-deployment alias uniqueness is explicitly reviewed

raw_body: The first increment SHALL keep configuration, deployment, updates and infrastructure changes human-operated. Handoffs SHALL identify the target, release, project, selected mode, intended writes and verification/rollback boundary before action. ### Requirement: Bind approvals to concrete human actions

The first increment SHALL keep configuration, deployment, updates and infrastructure changes human-operated. Handoffs SHALL identify the target, release, project, selected mode, intended writes and verification/rollback boundary before action. Existing authorization SHALL be honored within scope; changed targets or effects SHALL require renewed review. Read-only readiness SHALL never authorize deployment.

#### Scenario: Approve configuration without deployment

- **THEN** the handoff separates secret entry from the helper's start offer and the human declines startup until deployment is authorized

- **THEN** the agent presents the changed concrete action for review rather than replaying the prior approved command

### Requirement: Emit bounded machine-readable inspection results

Opt-in JSON inspection SHALL emit one versioned object containing operation, observed target identity, check statuses, stable codes, safe next actions and public-verification disposition. Missing observations SHALL remain unknown or not-run. Exit status SHALL distinguish readiness, known blocks, inspection failure and invalid invocation without changing legacy interactive exit semantics.

#### Scenario: Ready inspection result
- **WHEN** every applicable local prerequisite passes
- **THEN** JSON reports readiness only, with public verification not-run and installation completion false

#### Scenario: Failed dependency inspection
- **WHEN** a bounded check times out or its result cannot be established
- **THEN** JSON reports that check as blocked or failed, later dependent checks as not-run and a safe human next action

#### Scenario: Machine output discipline
- **WHEN** JSON mode is requested
- **THEN** stdout contains exactly one parseable object with no prompts, secret values or child-process progress mixed into it

title: Resume by reinspection instead of replay
raw_body: A resumed agent session SHALL establish current release, configuration and target identity again, distinguish completed human steps from unknown outcomes and select the next safe handoff. It SHALL NOT automatically repeat setup, deployment, migration or rollback. A changed input during inspection SHALL invalidate readiness rather than attach success to mixed observations.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Resume by reinspection instead of replay

A resumed agent session SHALL establish current release, configuration and target identity again, distinguish completed human steps from unknown outcomes and select the next safe handoff. It SHALL NOT automatically repeat setup, deployment, migration or rollback. A changed input during inspection SHALL invalidate readiness rather than attach success to mixed observations.

#### Scenario: Configuration saved but startup skipped
- **WHEN** a prior human session saved configuration and declined or could not perform startup
- **THEN** reinspection preserves that configuration and reports startup/public verification incomplete instead of treating setup exit zero as installation success

#### Scenario: Interrupted update outcome unknown
- **WHEN** a prior update may have reached migration or recreation before interruption
- **THEN** assistance stops at operator diagnosis under the existing update/recovery guidance and does not retry or change image tags automatically

#### Scenario: Inputs change during inspection
- **WHEN** relevant project/configuration inputs change before inspection finishes
- **THEN** the result reports changed inputs and requires reinspection without claiming a consistent readiness result

### Requirement: Report installation evidence without upgrading its meaning

The final handoff SHALL distinguish prepared configuration, static validation, disposable runtime tests and observed target-host behavior. Public HTTPS health, login, assets, API routing, authenticated SSE and persistence after recreation SHALL retain individual observed or unrun outcomes. Backup/schema/recovery qualification SHALL remain separate; Compose success or administrative issue closure SHALL NOT certify it.

- **THEN** the report states local checks passed and public behavior not-run, with no installed-and-working claim

#### Scenario: Partial public verification
- **WHEN** health succeeds but login, SSE or recreation has not been observed
- **THEN** the handoff records the individual outcomes and overall partial completion

#### Scenario: Backup evidence acknowledged
- **WHEN** the updater accepts a nonempty backup report file
- **THEN** assistance reports only that acknowledgement and leaves recoverability unverified; administrative issue closure does not change that evidence

- **WHEN** recovery chooses Tomorrow for a day from Monday through Saturday
- **THEN** a same-week Tomorrow operation with explicit source index commits before replacement assignment starts

#### Scenario: Sunday or next-week choice
- **WHEN** recovery chooses Tomorrow on Sunday or Save for Next Week on any day

- **AND** an earlier free slot in October 19–25 is not selected for the prior recipe

- **THEN** the prior recipe's destination search begins at offset one

- **WHEN** recovery captures reference Monday October 12 and source October 21 at offset one, but requests complete after deployment Monday October 19 begins
- **THEN** deferral still starts October 26 and replacement still targets October 21

title: Guard recovery assignment against occupied supper slots
raw_body: POST /api/schedule/assign SHALL accept optional boolean requireEmpty, default false. When true, it SHALL require an explicit valid reference Monday and dayIndex zero through six, and atomically assign only if no calendar entry exists at the resolved date's supper slot zero. - **WHEN** requireEmpty is true and a supper entry exists for another recipe, the chosen recipe, non-cooking content or a completed meal
- **THEN** the response is 409 and calendar entries, weekly plans, groceries and publication state are unchanged by that rejected invocation

#### Scenario: Sunday conflict cannot carry forward
- **WHEN** a guarded Sunday assignment finds an existing supper entry and following Monday is occupied
- **THEN** it returns 409 without changing either date or carrying any recipe forward

#### Scenario: Competing guarded saves
- **WHEN** two guarded assignments race to save different recipes into the same empty supper slot
- **THEN** at most one commits, the other returns 409, and only one supper entry exists without displacement

#### Scenario: Invalid captured target
- **WHEN** a guarded request omits its reference, uses a malformed or non-Monday reference, or has dayIndex outside zero through six
- **THEN** it returns 400 without changing any calendar entry or weekly plan

#### Scenario: Another meal slot exists
- **WHEN** only a non-supper entry exists on the target date and guarded supper assignment succeeds
- **THEN** that other entry is unchanged and the new supper entry uses meal slot zero

#### Scenario: Legacy caller
- **WHEN** requireEmpty is omitted or false
- **THEN** the existing assignment replacement, Sunday carry-forward, response and failure behavior remain unchanged

title: Order Quick Find pools by live then historical interest
raw_body: Quick Find and Quick Replace SHALL fill at most five unique recipes from eligible current live-liked candidates first, qualifying four-week historical liked-but-unselected candidates second, then existing Discovery fallback candidates. Each pool SHALL exclude IDs already selected. Existing hard constraints, target-week assignment exclusion and effective persisted cooked cooldown SHALL apply. Live eligibility SHALL include supported early votes without a VotingOpen gate.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Order Quick Find pools by live then historical interest

Quick Find and Quick Replace SHALL fill at most five unique recipes from eligible current live-liked candidates first, qualifying four-week historical liked-but-unselected candidates second, then existing Discovery fallback candidates. Each pool SHALL exclude IDs already selected. Existing hard constraints, target-week assignment exclusion and effective persisted cooked cooldown SHALL apply. Live eligibility SHALL include supported early votes without a VotingOpen gate.

#### Scenario: All three pools contribute
- **WHEN** two eligible live-liked recipes, two additional historical recipes and fallback recipes exist
- **THEN** results contain the two live recipes first, the two historical recipes next, and one fallback last

#### Scenario: Live likes outrank history
- **WHEN** eligible A has current live likes and eligible B has only qualifying historical interest
- **THEN** A precedes B regardless of B's historical count

#### Scenario: Full live deck
- **WHEN** six eligible live-liked recipes and historical candidates exist
- **THEN** the first five live-liked recipes fill the deck; history and fallback receive no reserved slots

#### Scenario: History leads without live likes
- **WHEN** no live-liked candidate qualifies and six historical candidates qualify
- **THEN** the first five historical candidates fill the deck

#### Scenario: Historical and current liked
- **WHEN** A belongs to live-liked, historical and Discovery pools
- **THEN** A appears once in the live pool and consumes one of five slots

#### Scenario: No history
- **WHEN** no historical candidate qualifies
- **THEN** existing live-liked then Discovery fallback ordering fills the available slots subject to accepted constraints

#### Scenario: Neither interest signal
- **WHEN** neither live nor historical candidates qualify
- **THEN** existing eligible fallback candidates fill up to five slots

#### Scenario: Early votes before opening
- **WHEN** valid live likes arrive after the previous close but before the next week explicitly opens
- **THEN** eligible liked recipes participate in the first pool without a VotingOpen status gate

#### Scenario: Votes cleared
- **WHEN** close clears current votes and A has qualifying historical unselected interest
- **THEN** A can enter the second pool without a new vote; with no eligible live recipes that pool leads

#### Scenario: Hard exclusion
- **WHEN** a live-liked or historically liked recipe is assigned in the target week, unavailable or in effective persisted cooked cooldown
- **THEN** it is excluded even if fewer than five alternatives remain

#### Scenario: Manual Discovery off
- **WHEN** a ready unassigned live-liked or historical recipe is manually outside Discovery but not under effective cooked suppression
- **THEN** that fact alone does not newly exclude it from those pools; the Discovery fallback retains its own eligibility

The live-liked pool SHALL retain never-cooked first, then oldest cooked date, then current like count descending, with stable identity for remaining ties. - **THEN** the higher current-like candidate comes first

#### Scenario: Historical-only intensity
- **WHEN** historical-only A had five historical likes and B one, with equal cooked-date position
- **THEN** identity resolves the tie without adding historical counts to current likes

#### Scenario: Deterministic repeat
- **WHEN** all eligible candidate facts remain unchanged
- **THEN** repeated reads return the same ordered set of at most five unique IDs

Recomputation SHALL retain existing week status or create a missing Draft plan. A missing entry SHALL complete without those follow-ups. Completed deletion SHALL return 204 without a body.

- **WHEN** clear finds no entry at its date
- **THEN** it returns 204 without invoking those follow-ups

#### Scenario: Later clear work fails
- **WHEN** a follow-up throws after the entry was deleted
- **THEN** clear does not return successful completion through that invocation, without establishing restoration of the entry

#### Scenario: Clear creates a missing weekly plan
- **WHEN** the entry is deleted with no containing weekly plan and recomputation persistence succeeds
- **THEN** the follow-up creates a Draft weekly plan for that Monday

#### Scenario: Clear retains existing week status

title: Apply the shared date-delete lifecycle to recipe-backed entries
raw_body: Recipe-backed removal SHALL use the same protected date-only DELETE and persistence-before-follow-up lifecycle as the accepted Delete the recipe-free entry before clear follow-up work requirement. It SHALL remove the selected calendar entry rather than delete the recipe. It SHALL add no expected-recipe, day-status or week-status precondition. Removing a Cooked entry SHALL recalculate that recipe's last-cooked value from remaining Cooked calendar dates before refresh work.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Apply the shared date-delete lifecycle to recipe-backed entries

Recipe-backed removal SHALL use the same protected date-only DELETE and persistence-before-follow-up lifecycle as the accepted Delete the recipe-free entry before clear follow-up work requirement. It SHALL remove the selected calendar entry rather than delete the recipe. It SHALL add no expected-recipe, day-status or week-status precondition. Removing a Cooked entry SHALL recalculate that recipe's last-cooked value from remaining Cooked calendar dates before refresh work.

#### Scenario: Recipe-backed date exists
- **WHEN** the selected date contains a recipe-backed entry and deletion persistence succeeds
- **THEN** that entry is removed, while the recipe remains available and the accepted recompute/publication sequence follows

#### Scenario: No calendar entry exists
- **WHEN** the date is already empty
- **THEN** deletion returns 204 without invoking the existing-entry follow-up sequence

#### Scenario: Correct a cooked meal with earlier history
- **WHEN** the latest Cooked assignment is removed and an earlier Cooked calendar entry remains for that recipe
- **THEN** its last-cooked value becomes that earlier calendar date at midnight UTC
- **AND** assigning and marking the actual replacement Cooked uses the existing completion operation independently

#### Scenario: Remove the only cooked occurrence
- **WHEN** a recipe's only Cooked assignment is removed
- **THEN** its last-cooked value becomes null before follow-up publication

#### Scenario: Remove an ordinary planned entry
- **WHEN** a Planned entry is removed
- **THEN** removal does not change its recipe's last-cooked value

title: Activate Planner dragging after a deliberate hold
raw_body: The Planner drag handle SHALL always wait for an uninterrupted 250 millisecond hold before starting for an eligible primary-button pointer, show grabbed feedback on activation, and request a brief vibration when the browser supplies that facility. This behavior SHALL NOT depend on a feature-flag snapshot, deployment variable or saved member override. Secondary-button and explicitly non-primary pointers SHALL not start a hold.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Activate Planner dragging after a deliberate hold

The Planner drag handle SHALL always wait for an uninterrupted 250 millisecond hold before starting for an eligible primary-button pointer, show grabbed feedback on activation, and request a brief vibration when the browser supplies that facility. This behavior SHALL NOT depend on a feature-flag snapshot, deployment variable or saved member override. Secondary-button and explicitly non-primary pointers SHALL not start a hold.

#### Scenario: Hold reaches activation
- **WHEN** an eligible pointer remains pending for 250 milliseconds without cancellation
- **THEN** dragging starts once and the handle shows grabbed feedback, with a vibration request when supported

#### Scenario: Retired preview state is absent or stale
- **WHEN** feature flags are absent, loading or failed, or a legacy hold-to-move override was disabled
- **THEN** an eligible pointer still requires the deliberate hold and can activate movement

#### Scenario: Ineligible pointer
- **WHEN** a secondary-button or explicitly non-primary pointer presses the handle
- **THEN** that press does not start dragging or a pending hold

title: Cancel pending Planner holds before drag activation
raw_body: A pending Planner hold SHALL cancel when its pointer moves more than eight pixels from the press position, its pointer ends or cancels, another pointer begins, the window loses focus, or a pre-activation touch movement occurs on the handle. A cancelled hold SHALL not later activate from its retired timer. Removing the handle SHALL also retire pending activation.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Cancel pending Planner holds before drag activation

A pending Planner hold SHALL cancel when its pointer moves more than eight pixels from the press position, its pointer ends or cancels, another pointer begins, the window loses focus, or a pre-activation touch movement occurs on the handle. A cancelled hold SHALL not later activate from its retired timer. Removing the handle SHALL also retire pending activation.

#### Scenario: Scroll movement before activation
- **WHEN** a pending pointer moves more than eight pixels or the handle receives touch movement before activation
- **THEN** the pending hold is cancelled without preventing that pre-activation touch movement through the handle

#### Scenario: Release or interruption
- **WHEN** a pending hold receives its pointer end or cancellation, another pointer begins, or the window loses focus
- **THEN** waiting beyond the hold duration does not start dragging from that hold

#### Scenario: Handle unmounts
- **WHEN** the handle unmounts while a hold is pending
- **THEN** the previous pending activation is retired

The Planner drag handle SHALL be keyboard focusable and expose its localized hold guidance as an accessible name. A boundary key press SHALL submit no movement.

title: Preserve the Tomorrow supper chain across weeks
raw_body: Tomorrow SHALL move the exact source supper to the next deployment-calendar date. Each contiguous occupied supper date from that destination SHALL move one day forward until the first empty supper slot, across as many weeks as required. No two-week cap, swap fallback or silent no-op success SHALL apply. Other meal slots SHALL remain unchanged.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Preserve the Tomorrow supper chain across weeks

Tomorrow SHALL move the exact source supper to the next deployment-calendar date. Each contiguous occupied supper date from that destination SHALL move one day forward until the first empty supper slot, across as many weeks as required. No two-week cap, swap fallback or silent no-op success SHALL apply. Other meal slots SHALL remain unchanged.

#### Scenario: Sunday and two following weeks are occupied
- **WHEN** Sunday contains A and every supper date in the next two weeks is occupied, with the following Monday empty
- **THEN** A moves to the first Monday, each displaced entry moves exactly one day and the last entry reaches the third Monday without loss

#### Scenario: First gap ends the chain
- **WHEN** Tomorrow encounters occupied Monday and Tuesday, empty Wednesday and occupied Thursday
- **THEN** Monday and Tuesday move one day forward and Thursday remains unchanged

title: Resolve the current member through the API
raw_body: For an authorized household API request, GET `/api/family/me` SHALL resolve the member from a valid GUID in `X-Family-Member-Id`, falling back to the `x-family-member-id` cookie if the header is absent or not a valid GUID. For an existing member it SHALL return that member's profile in the `data` envelope. With neither a valid header nor a valid cookie identity it SHALL return 401.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Resolve the current member through the API

For an authorized household API request, GET `/api/family/me` SHALL resolve the member from a valid GUID in `X-Family-Member-Id`, falling back to the `x-family-member-id` cookie if the header is absent or not a valid GUID. For an existing member it SHALL return that member's profile in the `data` envelope. With neither a valid header nor a valid cookie identity it SHALL return 401.

#### Scenario: Header identity takes precedence
- **WHEN** an authorized request supplies a valid header GUID identifying an existing member and a cookie identifying a different member
- **THEN** the API returns the header-selected member's profile in `data`

#### Scenario: Cookie supplies the member identity
- **WHEN** an authorized request has no valid GUID in the identity header and supplies a cookie GUID identifying an existing member
- **THEN** the API returns the cookie-selected member's profile in `data`

#### Scenario: No parseable member identity is supplied
- **WHEN** an authorized request supplies neither a valid identity header GUID nor a valid identity cookie GUID
- **THEN** the current-member API returns 401

### Requirement: Recover identity when the protected client has no selection

When a protected page reaches client identity validation with neither an active selection nor a readable member cookie, the application SHALL attempt current-member API recovery. ### Requirement: Persist contract-valid member preference updates

title: Reconcile a single client preference save with its response
raw_body: For a loaded member, a single preference save SHALL optimistically update that member, replace it with the returned profile on success, and restore its prior profile and record an error on rejection. If the member is absent locally it SHALL return without sending the save. A response without a member ID SHALL count as a failed save.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Reconcile a single client preference save with its response

For a loaded member, a single preference save SHALL optimistically update that member, replace it with the returned profile on success, and restore its prior profile and record an error on rejection. If the member is absent locally it SHALL return without sending the save. A response without a member ID SHALL count as a failed save.

- **THEN** the prior loaded profile is restored and an error is recorded

title: Load a member preview snapshot and clear previous choices
raw_body: On protected-app member selection, the client SHALL clear its preview snapshot and load flags for that selection. With no selected member it SHALL keep an empty snapshot without a request. Window focus SHALL refresh the selected member's snapshot. While absent or loading, a feature with no enabled snapshot entry SHALL resolve disabled.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Load a member preview snapshot and clear previous choices

On protected-app member selection, the client SHALL clear its preview snapshot and load flags for that selection. With no selected member it SHALL keep an empty snapshot without a request. Window focus SHALL refresh the selected member's snapshot. While absent or loading, a feature with no enabled snapshot entry SHALL resolve disabled.

title: Recover from preview load and save failures
raw_body: A failed snapshot load SHALL clear flags and display a load-error alert with Retry in Settings. An ordinary save failure SHALL retain the confirmed choice, release pending state and offer retry feedback for that flag. A 409 save conflict SHALL refresh the snapshot and release the pending flag even if that refresh fails.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Recover from preview load and save failures

A failed snapshot load SHALL clear flags and display a load-error alert with Retry in Settings. An ordinary save failure SHALL retain the confirmed choice, release pending state and offer retry feedback for that flag. A 409 save conflict SHALL refresh the snapshot and release the pending flag even if that refresh fails.

#### Scenario: Snapshot load fails and retries
- **WHEN** loading the member snapshot fails
- **THEN** absent flags resolve disabled and Settings displays an alert with Retry that requests another snapshot

#### Scenario: Save rejects
- **WHEN** a preview save rejects without 409
- **THEN** the confirmed choice remains, the switch becomes available again and save-error feedback offers another attempt

#### Scenario: Deployment changes during save
- **WHEN** a save returns 409
- **THEN** the client refreshes flags and clears pending state whether the refresh succeeds or fails

After overdue persistence completes, finalization SHALL read and attempt a snapshot for each distinct affected Monday using its deployment-calendar-relative offset and no request exclusion identity. It SHALL not recompute groceries through this path. With no matching overdue entries it SHALL return without saves or publications through this invocation. Delivery SHALL remain household-live-updates-owned.

- **THEN** the invocation returns without performing finalization saves or snapshot publication

#### Scenario: Publication fails after completion save
- **WHEN** an affected-week read or publication throws after persistence
- **THEN** the invocation fails without establishing reversal of saved Cooked states or publication of remaining weeks

title: Close atomically with retry-safe round ownership
raw_body: Close SHALL capture the intended round and persisted plan, commit its aggregate snapshot and lock, and clear that round once as one durable outcome. A failed persistence boundary SHALL leave the round votes available. A retry after committed close SHALL return or recover that outcome without clearing later votes.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Close atomically with retry-safe round ownership

Close SHALL capture the intended round and persisted plan, commit its aggregate snapshot and lock, and clear that round once as one durable outcome. A failed persistence boundary SHALL leave the round votes available. A retry after committed close SHALL return or recover that outcome without clearing later votes.

#### Scenario: Snapshot failure
- **WHEN** snapshot persistence fails before close commit
- **THEN** no lock/history/clear partial outcome is committed; votes can be retried

#### Scenario: Lost response
- **WHEN** close commits but its response is lost; early votes arrive and the same close is retried
- **THEN** the retry recognizes completion and preserves every later vote

#### Scenario: Publication failure
- **WHEN** close commits but SSE publication fails
- **THEN** durable state remains closed; retry/reload can recover it without duplicate history or clearing

#### Scenario: Late vote
- **WHEN** a vote races the serialized close boundary
- **THEN** it is included in the closed snapshot and cleared, or retained as a next-round vote, never silently lost

#### Scenario: Concurrent closes
- **WHEN** two closes target the same round
- **THEN** one durable close outcome is produced; neither can replace history with an empty retry

#### Scenario: Reopen versus stale close
- **WHEN** a closed week reopens and a stale close request from the prior round arrives
- **THEN** the stale request cannot close or clear the new round

#### Scenario: Pending browser suggestion
- **WHEN** a displayed suggestion has not been persisted when close takes its plan snapshot
- **THEN** it is not selected in history; browser promotion remains its existing separate operation

### Requirement: Preserve one operational round across open and close

Opening a week SHALL preserve votes received since the previous completed close. Opening another week while a different week owns the active round SHALL fail without moving or clearing votes. These rules SHALL NOT make live vote rows persistent week-owned preferences.

- **THEN** only one obtains the round; the other request reports conflict without changing votes

#### Scenario: Same week open retry
- **WHEN** the active week receives the same open again
- **THEN** the operation is idempotent and retains votes

raw_body: An owned round SHALL remain VotingOpen after convergence. Only existing explicit closing operations SHALL promote suggestions, lock the week and capture historical interest through their existing boundaries. ### Requirement: Distinguish an open converged round from a closed week

An owned round SHALL remain VotingOpen after convergence. Only existing explicit closing operations SHALL promote suggestions, lock the week and capture historical interest through their existing boundaries. Convergence SHALL NOT clear votes, create assignments, capture history or alter Other plans. Existing Close Voting and Ask the Family controls SHALL remain the lifecycle controls.

- **WHEN** confirmed coverage meets the active week's required slots

#### Scenario: Another member occupies a pending destination

- **THEN** promotion preserves the newer occupied date, reports the conflict through existing failure handling and reconciles the captured week without issuing lock from that failed invocation

- **THEN** existing round-receipt recovery remains valid and retry cannot clear newer-round early votes or replace history with an empty snapshot

### Requirement: Reopen only for remaining meal capacity

The existing close-then-open flow SHALL retain saved meals and Other plans, preserve valid early votes, and evaluate the new round against its own remaining slots. Convergence from the previous round SHALL NOT stop a new round prematurely. Clearing a saved entry after close SHALL NOT itself reopen voting or automatically refill it.

#### Scenario: Replace one meal through a new round
- **WHEN** a user closes a full week, removes one saved meal and invokes Ask the Family for that week
- **THEN** the new round requires one distinct eligible match, leaves all other persisted dates unchanged, and stops Discovery when that match is confirmed

- **WHEN** the new round is closed
- **THEN** existing touched-row historical replacement and untouched-row preservation apply; no separate per-member history or new historical accumulator is introduced

- **WHEN** a user clears a recipe or Other plan after close without opening voting
- **THEN** the slot stays empty for existing Quick Find or Search recovery and no voting obligation is started

#### Scenario: Early votes before opening
- **WHEN** votes arrive after a completed close but before another week opens
- **THEN** they are recorded normally and retained when the chosen week acquires the existing single operational round

title: Keep convergence latched during a host lifetime
raw_body: On the supported single-host deployment, a converged round SHALL remain Discovery-stopped for that round throughout the host lifetime, even when later votes or plan edits change coverage. raw_block:
### Requirement: Keep convergence latched during a host lifetime

On the supported single-host deployment, a converged round SHALL remain Discovery-stopped for that round throughout the host lifetime, even when later votes or plan edits change coverage. Explicit close and subsequent open SHALL establish the next round. Failed reads and repeated opens of the same round SHALL NOT reset convergence.

#### Scenario: Later plan edit frees capacity
- **WHEN** a date is freed after convergence while the same host and round remain active
- **THEN** informational capacity updates but Discovery remains stopped and the slot is not automatically assigned

#### Scenario: Match is withdrawn
- **WHEN** an otherwise valid replacement vote reduces consensus after convergence
- **THEN** current suggestions reconcile while Discovery remains stopped within that host round

#### Scenario: Same open request repeats
- **WHEN** opening the currently owned week is retried without closing
- **THEN** the round retains its stop decision and votes; the retry does not manufacture a new session

title: Rehydrate voting from existing persisted data
raw_body: After host restart, session state SHALL be reconstructed from existing votes, round ownership and persisted schedule data without a new durable convergence marker. Coverage SHALL be recalculated. Discovery SHALL resume if the reconstructed owned round no longer has enough matches. raw_block:
### Requirement: Rehydrate voting from existing persisted data

After host restart, session state SHALL be reconstructed from existing votes, round ownership and persisted schedule data without a new durable convergence marker. Coverage SHALL be recalculated. Discovery SHALL resume if the reconstructed owned round no longer has enough matches. With no week owner, ordinary early voting SHALL remain available without assuming week zero owns voting.

#### Scenario: Restart with sufficient coverage
- **WHEN** the host restarts and the stored owned round still has sufficient confirmed coverage
- **THEN** the hydrated session reports convergence without requiring another vote

#### Scenario: Restart after changed inputs
- **WHEN** an earlier converged round has insufficient current coverage after host restart
- **THEN** Discovery resumes for that round from current data, as the explicit exception to host-lifetime latching

#### Scenario: Hydration fails
- **WHEN** required database reads fail
- **THEN** the session is unavailable rather than fabricated as empty or converged, and later reads can retry hydration without discarding votes

#### Scenario: No week owns early votes
- **WHEN** hydration finds early votes and no active week owner
- **THEN** those votes remain available for a later open and no target or celebration is inferred from the currently viewed Planner week

- **THEN** the screen returns to the primary capture controls and clears the URL review draft

### Requirement: Initial recipe creation and workflow dispatch

Upon accepting a URL capture request, the API SHALL persist an initial recipe entity in the library database and disk store with default placeholder name, provided notes, rating, source URL, and database readiness set to false, then request the background URL import workflow. A caught dispatch failure SHALL leave the persisted recipe pending and still return its intake identity.

#### Scenario: Initial recipe stored with pending readiness
- **WHEN** the API accepts POST `/api/recipes/capture-url`
- **THEN** it creates a database recipe and initial recipe info file with database `IsReady = false`, `ImageCount = 0`, and `IsDiscoverable = false`
- **AND** it requests the background `url-import` workflow with the recipe ID and URL

#### Scenario: Dispatch fails after initial persistence
- **WHEN** the recipe is persisted but its background dispatch throws
- **THEN** the intake identity is still returned and the stored recipe remains pending
- **AND** acceptance alone does not establish an executing workflow

### Requirement: Background web acquisition and recipe extraction

When acquisition executes, the system SHALL attempt to fetch source HTML and obtain recipe context. After successful context processing, it SHALL retain the source URL and acquired HTML. A supplied hero URL SHALL be attempted without making hero download success a prerequisite. Recipe extraction SHALL persist normalized content only after semantic validation succeeds.

#### Scenario: Fetch webpage content and hero image
- **WHEN** the acquisition task executes for a recipe URL
- **THEN** after successful context processing it retains the source URL and HTML, uses a host-based title fallback if no title is returned, and attempts download only when a hero URL is supplied

#### Scenario: Scraping forbidden fallback
- **WHEN** fetching the source URL returns HTTP 403 Forbidden
- **THEN** the acquisition logs a warning and context processing proceeds with empty HTML and uses the URL host as a title fallback when no title is returned

#### Scenario: AI-assisted extraction and semantic validation
- **WHEN** recipe extraction runs against source HTML
- **THEN** it validates candidate structured content for a name, ingredients and usable instruction steps before normalizing and persisting it
- **AND** an invalid final candidate fails extraction rather than certifying successful capture

- **THEN** the intake identity is still returned and the stored recipe remains pending

- **THEN** the provider request asks for that description in the configured language

### Requirement: Order discovery by likes and cooking recency

Queue reads SHALL order by descending like count, then by last-cooked date ascending with never-cooked recipes before dated recipes at the same count. Equal remaining keys SHALL use H descending from weekly-household-interest, then stable recipe identity. Historical signal SHALL not change live like counts or consensus.

#### Scenario: Higher interest

- **WHEN** recipes differ in like count
- **THEN** the higher-count recipe comes first regardless of cooking date

#### Scenario: Equal interest

- **WHEN** equal-count recipes include never-cooked, older-cooked and newer-cooked recipes
- **THEN** they appear in that sequence

raw_body: Successful authorized GET `/api/recipes` with `order=explore` SHALL order eligible records with never-cooked first, then oldest cooked date, then H descending from weekly-household-interest, newest creation time and stable identity. raw_block:
### Requirement: Return an explore-ordered library page

Successful authorized GET `/api/recipes` with `order=explore` SHALL order eligible records with never-cooked first, then oldest cooked date, then H descending from weekly-household-interest, newest creation time and stable identity. It SHALL return the requested offset page in `recipes`, with `updatedAt` and `pagination` containing page, limit and filtered total, outside a `data` envelope. Page SHALL be at least 1 and limit SHALL be clamped to 1–100.

#### Scenario: Explore ordering
- **WHEN** an authorized lowercase-explore request succeeds for eligible recipes with differing cooked dates or creation times
- **THEN** never-cooked records precede cooked records, older cooked dates precede newer ones, and H descending, then creation time descending and identity order records with the same cooked-date position

#### Scenario: Page response and count
- **WHEN** an authorized explore request with page 2 and limit 12 succeeds
- **THEN** `recipes` contains up to 12 eligible records after the first 12 in explore order
- **AND** the unwrapped response includes `updatedAt` and pagination page 2, limit 12 and the eligible filtered total

#### Scenario: Page bounds are normalized
- **WHEN** an authorized explore request supplies page below 1 or limit outside 1–100 and succeeds
- **THEN** the response uses page at least 1 and limit clamped to 1–100

title: Display successfully returned library items
raw_body: After a successful first-page load in list presentation, the library SHALL replace its loaded items with the returned records and display them as named recipe buttons with a hero-image reference and formatted total time. Activating a recipe button SHALL request that recipe's detail sheet.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Display successfully returned library items

After a successful first-page load in list presentation, the library SHALL replace its loaded items with the returned records and display them as named recipe buttons with a hero-image reference and formatted total time. Activating a recipe button SHALL request that recipe's detail sheet.

#### Scenario: Display a returned page
- **WHEN** a first-page list load succeeds with nonempty returned records
- **THEN** the list displays the returned recipes by name with image references and formatted time
- **AND** activating a displayed recipe requests its detail sheet

title: Request and append additional library list pages
raw_body: When list scrolling reaches within 600 pixels of the bottom and more pages are indicated with no initial load or page request pending, the library SHALL request the next page using the current filter and list page size. A successful append SHALL retain loaded items and add returned records with previously unseen nonempty IDs in response order.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Request and append additional library list pages

When list scrolling reaches within 600 pixels of the bottom and more pages are indicated with no initial load or page request pending, the library SHALL request the next page using the current filter and list page size. A successful append SHALL retain loaded items and add returned records with previously unseen nonempty IDs in response order.

#### Scenario: Scroll requests the next page
- **WHEN** list scrolling reaches the loading threshold with more pages indicated and no load pending
- **THEN** the library requests the next page with explore ordering, limit 12 and the current discoverable filter

#### Scenario: Append overlapping results
- **WHEN** a subsequent page succeeds containing an already loaded ID and previously unseen nonempty IDs
- **THEN** loaded items remain and the new IDs are appended in response order without appending the repeated ID

title: Offer retry after initial library-load failure
raw_body: If the summary or first-page recipe request fails, the library SHALL display “Failed to load recipes.” and a Retry control. Retry SHALL request the current filter's first-page load again, including summary retrieval, with loading feedback. A successful retry SHALL replace the displayed result with its returned items or applicable All-mode empty feedback.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Offer retry after initial library-load failure

If the summary or first-page recipe request fails, the library SHALL display “Failed to load recipes.” and a Retry control. Retry SHALL request the current filter's first-page load again, including summary retrieval, with loading feedback. A successful retry SHALL replace the displayed result with its returned items or applicable All-mode empty feedback.

#### Scenario: Initial load fails
- **WHEN** the initial summary or first-page recipe request fails
- **THEN** the library shows failure feedback and Retry in place of the list result

#### Scenario: Retry succeeds
- **WHEN** a person activates Retry and the repeated summary and first-page requests succeed
- **THEN** the library shows loading feedback while pending and then displays the returned first page or applicable All-mode empty feedback

### Requirement: Report never-cooked and persisted rating counts

- **THEN** `neverCooked` is 2

title: Wrap stack navigation within available results
raw_body: For a stable collection, navigation SHALL fetch missing adjacent pages and reach every eligible recipe in both directions. Next at the collection end SHALL wrap to its first card. ### Requirement: Wrap stack navigation within available results

For a stable collection, navigation SHALL fetch missing adjacent pages and reach every eligible recipe in both directions. Next at the collection end SHALL wrap to its first card. ### Requirement: Queue bounded vegetarian classification batches

raw_block:

raw_body: The photo viewer SHALL support zooming and panning the displayed photo. Activating the zoom control or tapping the photo at fit-to-screen scale SHALL zoom to 2.5 scale, enable dragging within bounded constraints, and display “Fit to Screen”. Activating Fit to Screen or tapping a zoomed photo SHALL return scale to 1, disable dragging, and center the photo. The viewer SHALL clamp two-finger pinch touch gestures between scale 1 and 5.

### Requirement: Support photo zooming and panning

The photo viewer SHALL support zooming and panning the displayed photo. Activating the zoom control or tapping the photo at fit-to-screen scale SHALL zoom to 2.5 scale, enable dragging within bounded constraints, and display “Fit to Screen”. Activating Fit to Screen or tapping a zoomed photo SHALL return scale to 1, disable dragging, and center the photo. The viewer SHALL clamp two-finger pinch touch gestures between scale 1 and 5.

### Requirement: Reconcile cooked cooldown through Dreaming

Dreaming SHALL evaluate current cooked date, cooldown configuration, Human-off intent and supper suitability, then persist Discovery eligibility. #### Scenario: Cooked since prior run

- **THEN** reads retain persisted state until the next pass; that pass evaluates A using its then-current date

#### Scenario: Never eaten
- **WHEN** A has no cooked date
- **THEN** Dreaming applies no cooked cooldown, without asserting knowledge of unrecorded real-world meals

#### Scenario: Elapsed but not reconciled
- **WHEN** A ages beyond cooldown while Dreaming is delayed
- **THEN** it returns only after a successful reconciliation, not at an implied exact timer deadline

### Requirement: Keep rotation reasons independent

Persisted cooked-cooldown state, explicit persistent out-of-rotation intent and explicit supper suitability SHALL remain distinguishable. Cooldown expiry SHALL not reverse explicit persistent exclusion or unsuitable status. - **WHEN** an explicitly kept out of rotation recipe ages out of cooldown
- **THEN** it remains outside Discovery

#### Scenario: Quick Find reason
- **WHEN** A is Discovery-off solely by manual choice and B by cooked cooldown
- **THEN** the new cooldown gate excludes B; it does not newly exclude A from history/live-liked pools

#### Scenario: Unsuitable return

title: Recover repeated and partial Dreaming work safely

- **WHEN** A commits and B fails during a run

- **THEN** the stale restoration does not override the newer cooking facts

#### Scenario: Undo cooking
- **WHEN** the authoritative cooked date is corrected or cleared
- **THEN** next successful Dreaming uses the corrected value without inventing a new cooking event

#### Scenario: Duplicate scheduling
- **WHEN** two workflow deliveries process the same recipes
- **THEN** idempotent persistence and current-fact checks prevent conflicting final results

### Requirement: Classify search mode from normalized effective intent

#### Scenario: Empty request object

- **THEN** Search selects Explicit

- **WHEN** text and concepts are blank and one filter materially restricts eligible recipes
- **THEN** Search selects Explicit

- **WHEN** a source recipe identity is supplied with any combination of text, concepts or filters
- **THEN** Search selects Find Similar and never applies Discovery personalization

#### Scenario: Response reports the selected policy

- **WHEN** Search returns Discovery, Explicit or Find Similar results
- **THEN** response `searchMode` is respectively `discovery`, `explicit` or `similar`, never the legacy `standard` value

### Requirement: Preserve Explicit and Similar retrieval order

Explicit and Find Similar SHALL preserve their base retrieval order after hard eligibility filters. - **THEN** historical interest does not resolve their order

title: Produce reproducible offline relevance evidence
raw_body: The search evaluation SHALL use a versioned privacy-safe corpus with at least 40 development and 20 held-out English/French queries. Judgments SHALL be arm-independent grades 0, 1 or 2, with named hard negatives graded 0. Default evaluation SHALL make no external provider calls.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Produce reproducible offline relevance evidence

The search evaluation SHALL use a versioned privacy-safe corpus with at least 40 development and 20 held-out English/French queries. Judgments SHALL be arm-independent grades 0, 1 or 2, with named hard negatives graded 0. Default evaluation SHALL make no external provider calls.

#### Scenario: Development iteration

- **WHEN** an evaluator compares retrieval or qualification arms before held-out scoring
- **THEN** it uses only the development set and records the corpus, query set, configuration and random-seed identities

#### Scenario: Held-out decision

- **WHEN** held-out results are scored
- **THEN** labels, metric definitions, thresholds and tolerated slice regressions were frozen before arm identities were inspected

#### Scenario: Default local run

- **WHEN** repository validation runs without explicit provider authorization
- **THEN** evaluation uses committed privacy-safe fixtures and performs no paid or production provider call

### Requirement: Score relevance arms with fixed metrics

Evaluation SHALL report per-query macro candidate recall at the fused window, precision at 5, graded nDCG at 10, irrelevant-result rate, no-match false-positive rate and named hard-negative admission rate. Top Pick SHALL count as rank 1 exactly once. Critical language and intent slices SHALL be reported separately.

#### Scenario: Top Pick is present

- **WHEN** an evaluated response contains Top Pick and alternatives
- **THEN** Top Pick occupies rank 1 and is not counted again among alternatives

#### Scenario: True no-match query

- **WHEN** a query is judged to have no relevant corpus result
- **THEN** any returned candidate contributes to the no-match false-positive rate

#### Scenario: Slice regression

- **WHEN** an overall arm improves but a frozen critical slice exceeds its tolerated regression
- **THEN** the arm does not pass its decision gate

raw_body: With no similar target, no nonblank text, no usable preference concepts and no effective filters, Search SHALL return Discovery browse results without generating a query embedding. Candidates SHALL use recipe-library readiness/deletion facts and need not have a published search document. Effective filters SHALL select filter-only Explicit instead of personalized Discovery.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Choose browse only without usable search content

With no similar target, no nonblank text, no usable preference concepts and no effective filters, Search SHALL return Discovery browse results without generating a query embedding. Candidates SHALL use recipe-library readiness/deletion facts and need not have a published search document. Effective filters SHALL select filter-only Explicit instead of personalized Discovery.

#### Scenario: Blank content

- **WHEN** a request has whitespace text, only blank concepts and no effective filters without a similar target
- **THEN** the service follows Discovery browse without query embedding generation

#### Scenario: Empty filter representation

- **WHEN** an otherwise blank request supplies an empty filter object or only inactive filter values
- **THEN** the representation alone does not prevent Discovery browse

#### Scenario: Recipe not indexed

- **WHEN** an otherwise Discovery-eligible recipe has no search document

title: Retain cards and expose continuation retry or restart
raw_body: A continuation request failure for the current search generation SHALL retain loaded cards. A 409 SHALL expose Restart search, submitting a fresh initial request with current search context; other failures SHALL expose Load more retry using the cursor. These actions SHALL offer another attempt without promising successful recovery.

### Requirement: Retain cards and expose continuation retry or restart

A continuation request failure for the current search generation SHALL retain loaded cards. A 409 SHALL expose Restart search, submitting a fresh initial request with current search context; other failures SHALL expose Load more retry using the cursor. - **THEN** loaded cards remain and Restart search is offered

- **THEN** loaded cards remain and Load more retry is offered

title: Suppress obsolete search success without claiming network cancellation
raw_body: Initial, replacement and continuation successes SHALL be ignored when their captured search generation or promotion version no longer matches current state. The initial effect SHALL also ignore completion after its cleanup. These guards SHALL NOT establish cancellation of browser network requests or suppression of every obsolete failure presentation.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Suppress obsolete search success without claiming network cancellation

Initial, replacement and continuation successes SHALL be ignored when their captured search generation or promotion version no longer matches current state. The initial effect SHALL also ignore completion after its cleanup. These guards SHALL NOT establish cancellation of browser network requests or suppression of every obsolete failure presentation.

#### Scenario: Older initial browse finishes

- **WHEN** a newer text search has already advanced the search generation
- **THEN** the old initial success cannot replace the newer results

#### Scenario: Old continuation finishes

- **WHEN** a replacement search or promotion invalidation occurred before continuation success
- **THEN** that success is not appended to current data

title: Restart mounted browse after received promotion invalidation
raw_body: When mounted Search observes a newer promotion generation, it SHALL withhold obsolete cards and refresh browse, typed and Similar results using current query, filters, preferences, similar target and planner context. This SHALL also apply while an initial or replacement request is pending. Invalidation delivery remains with household-live-updates; server eligibility and ranking remain authoritative.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Restart mounted browse after received promotion invalidation

When mounted Search observes a newer promotion generation, it SHALL withhold obsolete cards and refresh browse, typed and Similar results using current query, filters, preferences, similar target and planner context. This SHALL also apply while an initial or replacement request is pending. Invalidation delivery remains with household-live-updates; server eligibility and ranking remain authoritative.

#### Scenario: Browse invalidated
- **WHEN** a mounted browse observes a newer promotion generation
- **THEN** old cards are withheld and a replacement initial request is scheduled with active context

#### Scenario: Ranked data invalidated
- **WHEN** a mounted typed or Similar response becomes obsolete
- **THEN** a replacement initial request retains current search context and displays its current successful results without retyping

#### Scenario: Invalidation before a response
- **WHEN** invalidation arrives during an initial or replacement request
- **THEN** a fresh request starts with current context and the obsolete request cannot replace its results or error presentation

#### Scenario: Repeated events and later typing
- **WHEN** another invalidation or new search supersedes a pending refresh
- **THEN** only current-generation outcomes are displayed; completed refreshes and later typing do not themselves repeat an already handled invalidation

title: Retry a failed initial or replacement search
raw_body: A current failed initial or replacement request SHALL show a search error and Retry instead of successful-empty guidance. Retry SHALL submit the current query, filters, preferences, similar target and planner context without requiring re-entry. A new request SHALL clear the prior error. Obsolete request failures SHALL NOT replace current results or errors.

### Requirement: Retry a failed initial or replacement search

A current failed initial or replacement request SHALL show a search error and Retry instead of successful-empty guidance. Retry SHALL submit the current query, filters, preferences, similar target and planner context without requiring re-entry. A new request SHALL clear the prior error. Obsolete request failures SHALL NOT replace current results or errors.

- **THEN** error and Retry replace loading, retained input is submitted again and current returned cards are displayed

title: Keep history stable across continuation
raw_body: Historical ranking SHALL apply only to Discovery and remain stable throughout a valid Discovery continuation chain. Explicit and Find Similar SHALL exclude history from ordering and preserve their initial ordered snapshots. A changed required generation SHALL preserve the compatible snapshot or cause explicit restart rather than silently append a reordered sequence.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Keep history stable across continuation

Historical ranking SHALL apply only to Discovery and remain stable throughout a valid Discovery continuation chain. Explicit and Find Similar SHALL exclude history from ordering and preserve their initial ordered snapshots. A changed required generation SHALL preserve the compatible snapshot or cause explicit restart rather than silently append a reordered sequence.

#### Scenario: Window turns Monday
- **WHEN** the historical window changes between Discovery pages
- **THEN** the chain uses its original historical inputs or requests restart without silent duplicates or omissions

#### Scenario: Revote between pages
- **WHEN** a closed historical week is updated after page one
- **THEN** the old Discovery chain is pinned or rejected for restart and existing cards remain until recovery

#### Scenario: Typed continuation
- **WHEN** an Explicit continuation loads after new history arrives
- **THEN** stored order is preserved and existing eligibility rechecks remain in force

#### Scenario: Similar continuation
- **WHEN** Find Similar continuation loads after household or planner preference facts change
- **THEN** stored similarity order is preserved

title: Present compact regular Search cards
raw_body: Regular Search cards SHALL use the compact Browse list presentation: edge-to-edge 4:3 images, small rounded corners, padded content with names visible up to two lines and readable formatted time. Narrow mobile layouts SHALL retain two columns with compact spacing. Supplied issue badges SHALL remain visible. Top Pick SHALL retain its distinct hero, reason and Surprise Me control.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Present compact regular Search cards

Regular Search cards SHALL use the compact Browse list presentation: edge-to-edge 4:3 images, small rounded corners, padded content with names visible up to two lines and readable formatted time. Narrow mobile layouts SHALL retain two columns with compact spacing. Supplied issue badges SHALL remain visible. Top Pick SHALL retain its distinct hero, reason and Surprise Me control.

#### Scenario: Narrow results with Top Pick

- **THEN** ordinary cards match Browse list image treatment and content spacing while Top Pick remains distinct
- **AND** long names occupy up to two lines and issue badges remain inside their images

#### Scenario: No Top Pick
- **WHEN** Search returns ordinary alternatives without a Top Pick
- **THEN** the same compact grid displays them in their returned order without inventing a promoted card

#### Scenario: Return from compact card detail
- **WHEN** a person opens a compact card and closes its detail
- **THEN** the mounted query, selections and cards retain their existing return behavior and compact geometry without a close-triggered search

title: Generate privacy-scrubbed portable export bundle
raw_body: Authorized GET `/api/recipes/{id}/share` with household access and member context SHALL return a version 1.0 portable bundle with source `wfs-share`. The bundle SHALL preserve core recipe content, structured instructions, and original images (capped at five). The bundle SHALL scrub personal ratings and notes by setting them to null, and SHALL omit internal entity identifiers and member attribution.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Generate privacy-scrubbed portable export bundle

Authorized GET `/api/recipes/{id}/share` with household access and member context SHALL return a version 1.0 portable bundle with source `wfs-share`. The bundle SHALL preserve core recipe content, structured instructions, and original images (capped at five). The bundle SHALL scrub personal ratings and notes by setting them to null, and SHALL omit internal entity identifiers and member attribution.

#### Scenario: Scrub personal notes and rating
- **WHEN** an authorized export request succeeds for a recipe containing household notes and a rating
- **THEN** the returned bundle sets both `notes` and `rating` to null in the exported recipe payload

#### Scenario: Preserve structured instructions and original images up to five
- **WHEN** an authorized export request succeeds for a recipe with structured instructions and multiple original images
- **THEN** the bundle preserves the HowToSections and steps, and includes up to five original images with MIME types and base64 payloads

#### Scenario: Wrap flat instruction strings in a default section
- **WHEN** an authorized export request succeeds for a recipe whose raw metadata stores flat instruction strings
- **THEN** the bundle wraps the steps inside a default section named Instructions

#### Scenario: Reject export when recipe lacks hero image
- **WHEN** an authorized export request is made for a recipe without a hero image in storage
- **THEN** the API returns 400 Bad Request indicating the recipe must have a hero image before it can be shared

#### Scenario: Reject export when member context header is missing
- **WHEN** a request is made to GET `/api/recipes/{id}/share` without member context
- **THEN** the API returns 400 Bad Request requiring member context

#### Scenario: Reject export when recipe is not found
- **WHEN** an authorized export request is made for a recipe identifier that does not exist
- **THEN** the API returns 404 Not Found

title: Deliver export bundle via native sharing with download fallback
raw_body: Activating the Share control SHALL display a persistent loading notice and request the export bundle. If native file sharing is available and permitted, the client SHALL deliver the bundle via native share. If the user cancels native sharing, the action SHALL return cleanly without error feedback or download. If native sharing is unsupported or fails with a non-cancellation error, the client SHALL trigger a file download fallback.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Deliver export bundle via native sharing with download fallback

Activating the Share control SHALL display a persistent loading notice and request the export bundle. If native file sharing is available and permitted, the client SHALL deliver the bundle via native share. If the user cancels native sharing, the action SHALL return cleanly without error feedback or download. If native sharing is unsupported or fails with a non-cancellation error, the client SHALL trigger a file download fallback.

#### Scenario: Native share dispatch when supported
- **WHEN** a person activates Share on a device supporting native file sharing with permission granted
- **THEN** the application requests the export bundle, displays a preparation toast, and presents the native sharing interface with the bundle file

#### Scenario: Cancellation of native share suppresses error and file download
- **WHEN** a person cancels or aborts the native share interface
- **THEN** the loading toast is removed, no error banner is displayed, and no file download is initiated

#### Scenario: Fallback to browser file download when native share is unavailable or fails
- **WHEN** native sharing is unsupported or throws a non-cancellation error
- **THEN** the application triggers a browser file download of the plain-text bundle file named with the slugified recipe name

#### Scenario: Present inline error feedback when bundle request fails
- **WHEN** the export bundle request fails with a network or server error
- **THEN** the loading toast is removed, the Share control is re-enabled, and the detail sheet displays an inline share error message

title: Parse and validate imported bundle file payload
raw_body: Selecting a bundle file SHALL read and parse its JSON content. If the file cannot be parsed as JSON, intake SHALL fail with unreadable file feedback. If the payload is missing required schema fields, contains an invalid source, or has malformed instruction structures or image payloads, intake SHALL fail with invalid bundle feedback.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Parse and validate imported bundle file payload

Selecting a bundle file SHALL read and parse its JSON content. If the file cannot be parsed as JSON, intake SHALL fail with unreadable file feedback. If the payload is missing required schema fields, contains an invalid source, or has malformed instruction structures or image payloads, intake SHALL fail with invalid bundle feedback.

#### Scenario: Successfully parse valid bundle payload
- **WHEN** a person selects a valid JSON recipe bundle file conforming to the required schema
- **THEN** the client parses the file and transitions to the bundle review state

#### Scenario: Reject unreadable non-JSON file
- **WHEN** a person selects a file whose content cannot be parsed as JSON
- **THEN** the capture view displays an error message indicating the recipe file could not be read and does not enter review

#### Scenario: Reject bundle with malformed schema or invalid image payloads
- **WHEN** a person selects a JSON file missing required recipe fields, having an unsupported bundle source, or containing invalid image payloads
- **THEN** the capture view displays an error message indicating the recipe file is not valid and clears any parsed bundle state

title: Display advisory warning for existing library duplicates
raw_body: During bundle preview preparation, the client SHALL query the library for existing recipes matching the bundle's recorded source recipe ID or name. If a match is found, the view SHALL display an advisory warning banner (`duplicate-recipe-warning`) indicating the recipe already exists, with a control to view the existing recipe. The warning SHALL NOT prevent the user from proceeding with import acceptance.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Display advisory warning for existing library duplicates

During bundle preview preparation, the client SHALL query the library for existing recipes matching the bundle's recorded source recipe ID or name. If a match is found, the view SHALL display an advisory warning banner (`duplicate-recipe-warning`) indicating the recipe already exists, with a control to view the existing recipe. The warning SHALL NOT prevent the user from proceeding with import acceptance.

#### Scenario: Display duplicate warning when recorded recipe ID matches existing recipe
- **WHEN** the bundle's recorded recipe ID matches an existing non-deleted recipe in the household library
- **THEN** the review screen displays an advisory warning banner stating the recipe already exists in the library

#### Scenario: Display duplicate warning when recipe name matches existing recipe
- **WHEN** the bundle lacks a matching recipe ID but its recipe name matches an existing library recipe
- **THEN** the review screen displays the advisory duplicate warning banner

#### Scenario: View existing recipe opens recipe detail overlay
- **WHEN** a person activates "View existing recipe" from the duplicate warning banner
- **THEN** the application opens the recipe detail sheet for the existing matching recipe

#### Scenario: Duplicate warning permits import acceptance
- **WHEN** the duplicate warning banner is visible and the person activates "Import recipe"
- **THEN** the client proceeds with submitting the bundle to the import endpoint without blocking

title: Reconcile extra rollover during Dreaming
raw_body: Each Dreaming run SHALL reconcile grocery-extra lineages through the deployment-calendar current Monday. It SHALL create exactly one occurrence for each missing elapsed week while the prior occurrence was unchecked and not removed, and SHALL leave checked, removed, current, and already-carried lineages unchanged.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Reconcile extra rollover during Dreaming

Each Dreaming run SHALL reconcile grocery-extra lineages through the deployment-calendar current Monday. It SHALL create exactly one occurrence for each missing elapsed week while the prior occurrence was unchecked and not removed, and SHALL leave checked, removed, current, and already-carried lineages unchanged.

#### Scenario: First Dreaming run after rollover
- **WHEN** Dreaming first runs after the deployment calendar enters a new Monday and an extra remained unchecked
- **THEN** the new current week receives exactly one carried occurrence and the prior occurrence remains an unchanged historical snapshot

#### Scenario: Dreaming runs again
- **WHEN** another Dreaming run reconciles the same current week
- **THEN** it creates no duplicate occurrence for a lineage already carried into that week

#### Scenario: Several weeks were missed
- **WHEN** Dreaming finds an unchecked lineage whose latest occurrence predates several elapsed Mondays
- **THEN** it materializes exactly one immutable snapshot for every missing elapsed week through the current Monday

#### Scenario: Lineage already ended
- **WHEN** the latest occurrence is checked or removed
- **THEN** Dreaming creates no successor for that lineage

title: Publish lexical content before optional embedding work
raw_body: Indexing eligible content SHALL persist canonical text, metadata, schema version, source fingerprint, lexical ready status and indexing time before generating an embedding. With no embedding provider it SHALL leave embedding status pending while preserving published lexical content.
raw_block:
### Requirement: Publish lexical content before optional embedding work

Indexing eligible content SHALL persist canonical text, metadata, schema version, source fingerprint, lexical ready status and indexing time before generating an embedding. With no embedding provider it SHALL leave embedding status pending while preserving published lexical content.

#### Scenario: Provider unavailable
- **WHEN** lexical publication succeeds and no embedding provider is supplied
- **THEN** the document remains lexical-ready with embedding pending

#### Scenario: Embedding succeeds
- **WHEN** the provider returns a nonempty vector and the stored source fingerprint still matches
- **THEN** indexing persists the vector with its model, matching embedding fingerprint and ready embedding status
